text_blocks.snippet: Losartan (Cozaar) is an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) used to treat high blood pressure, protect the kidneys in type 2 diabetes, and lower the risk of stroke. While generally well tolerated, it can cause several side effects.
These effects are usually mild, temporary, and often improve as your body adjusts:

list.snippet: Dizziness or lightheadedness (especially when standing up quickly due to lower blood pressure)
Headache (often during the first week or two)
Stomach upset, such as nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea
Upper respiratory tract infections or a stuffy/runny nose
Back or joint pain and muscle cramps

text_blocks.snippet: Serious Side Effects (Require Prompt Medical Attention)
Contact a doctor immediately or seek emergency care if you experience any of the following:

list.snippet: Angioedema (Severe Allergic Reaction): Swelling of the face, lips, tongue, throat, eyes, hands, or feet, or trouble breathing or swallowing. (Seek emergency help right away).
Severely Low Blood Pressure (Hypotension): Extreme dizziness, fainting, or blurry vision.
High Potassium Levels (Hyperkalemia): Muscle weakness, confusion, numbness or tingling, or a fast or irregular heartbeat.
Kidney Problems: Sudden decrease in the amount of urine, blood in the urine, or unexplained swelling in the ankles or hands.
Liver Problems: Yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice) or severe upper stomach pain.
